Given that $(-3,3)$ is the midpoint of the line segment $\overset{―}{PQ}$ above, find the values of $a$ and $b.$

$a=$
{{field-1}},
$\,b=$
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
The given points are ${{(a,b)}_{⏟}}_{\text{(}{x}_{1},\,{y}_{1})}$, ${{(0,1)}_{⏟}}_{\text{(}{x}_{2},\,{y}_{2})}$ and ${{(-3,3)}_{⏟}}_{\text{(}{x}_{m},\,{y}_{m})}.$

We use the midpoint formula as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}({x}_{m},{y}_{m}) & =(\frac{{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}}{2},\frac{{y}_{1}+{y}_{2}}{2}) \\ (-3,3) & =(\frac{a+0}{2},\frac{b+1}{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding $x$- and $y$-coordinates in the equation above gives us

$$
\begin{aligned}\{\begin{aligned}-3=\frac{a}{2} \\ 3=\frac{b+1}{2}\end{aligned}\,⇒\,\{\begin{aligned}a=-6 \\ b=5.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $a=-6$ and $b=5.$
